subject: Latent variable index and dimensions error

messages.author: 6fee017125c7bf75
messages.subject: Latent variable index and dimensions error
parts:
Hi!

I'm just starting to use nimble so please bear with me if this is a ridiculously simple question. I've made a function to determine the nearest grid cell to the latent variable location. It runs and compiles just fine but when I use it in the model I get an error.

Function: 
nearest <- nimbleFunction(
run = function(x1 = double(1), 
x2 = double(1),
y1 = double(1),
y2 = double(1)) {
dist <- numeric(length(y2))
for(i in 1:length(y2)) {
dist[i] <- sqrt(((x1 - y1[i]) ^2) + ((x2 - y2[i]) ^2))[1] }
id <- which(dist == min(dist))
return(id)
returnType(integer(1))
}
)

Model:
for (t in 2:TT){ 
cell[t] <- nearest(mu[t,1], mu[t,2], S_x, S_y) #nearest neighbour in S to mu[t]
cell.p[t] <- nearest(mu[t-1,1], mu[t-1,2], S_x, S_y) #nearest neighbour in S to mu[t-1]
delta.d[t] <- (dist[cell[t], cell.p[t]]) #distance between 2 locations - dist is standardized so I don't think I need to standardize delta.d
X.match[t] <- cell[t] #I likely don't need this 
mu[t,1] <- expit((beta1*x1[X.match[t]] + beta2*x2[X.match[t]] + beta3*x3[X.match[t]]) - (delta.d[t]/(delta.t[t]*phi)))
mu[t,2] <- expit((beta1*x1[X.match[t]] + beta2*x2[X.match[t]] + beta3*x3[X.match[t]]) - (delta.d[t]/(delta.t[t]*phi)))
#observation model
s_lon[t] ~ dt(mu = mu[t, 1], sigma = sigma_lon, df = nu_lon) 
s_lat[t] ~ dt(mu = mu[t, 2], sigma = sigma_lat, df = nu_lat) 

Error is: 
Error in genVarInfo3() : 
  Dimension of cell is 0, which does not match its usage in 'delta.d[t] <- (dist[cell[t], cell.p[t]])'.

Any help is much appreciated! 

Cheers

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Latent variable index and dimensions error
parts:
Hi Rowenna,

Great that you're getting started and reaching out with a question.

This error would come up if somewhere there is an inconsistency about the shape of `cell`.  Are you providing it in the inits list, and if so is it a vector (which it looks like it should be)?  Another way this might come up is if `cell` appears elsewhere in the model without brackets.

-Perry

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Latent variable index and dimensions error
parts:
Another possible issue here - although without being able to run your example it's difficult to fully diagnose - is that your function "nearest" returns a *vector* return value, that's what's specified by returnType(integer(1)).  This contrasts its usage, where the output of nearest() is stored into the *scalar* cell[t].

I feel like this shouldn't work, which could be manifesting itself as the error you're seeing (having to do with the dimensionality of cell, and the same might also happen with cell.p).

messages.subject: Re: Latent variable index and dimensions error

Oh nice catch, Daniel.  So the fix to that would be "returnType(integer(0))", which declares a scalar return value.  Further, all variables in models are represented as doubles, even if they will have integer values, so "returnType(double(0))" should work too.
-Perry
